title: "Global games / equilibrium selection"
toc: true
---

## What it is
Global games study equilibrium selection in coordination games by adding small private noise to information about fundamentals.

## What’s special
- Many coordination games have multiple equilibria (good/bad outcomes).
- Tiny informational frictions can select a unique equilibrium.
- Provides a disciplined way to talk about “which equilibrium happens” without arbitrary refinements.

## One example (currency-attack intuition)
A government defends a peg if fundamentals are strong; speculators attack if they expect others to attack.

Each speculator observes a noisy signal of the fundamental. If signals are slightly noisy, an equilibrium often takes a **threshold form**: attack if your signal is below a cutoff. The cutoff is pinned down endogenously, yielding a unique prediction.
